messages.subject: For Jarand Rystad | Energy Strategy, Government Affairs & Emerging Markets | Executive Proposal
messages.body:
Dear Mr. Rystad,

I am writing from Guyana, where I serve as Liaison Director, Social Responsibility at AGM Inc., part of Zijin Mining Group. My work spans government relations, regulatory coordination, ESG, stakeholder strategy and executive issue management inside a major resource operation.

Rystad Energy's global advisory platform is a strong fit with the problems I solve today: translating policy and regulatory developments into business decisions, connecting energy-transition strategy to operating realities and managing complex relationships across government, industry and institutional stakeholders. My experience also brings a perspective from one of the world's fastest-growing resource economies.

I prepared a Rystad Energy-specific Strategic Value Creation Proposal rather than sending a conventional CV alone. It sets out where I would add value across emerging-market advisory, government and stakeholder intelligence, energy-transition execution and strategic client development. My three-page Executive CV forms the final section.

I am open to relocation to Norway and employer-supported work authorization. My strongest fit would be a Director, Head, Partner-track or senior leadership mandate across Government Affairs, Energy Transition, Strategic Advisory, Emerging Markets, Client Strategy or External Affairs.

I would value a short confidential conversation. If another senior leader owns the most relevant mandate, I would be grateful if you would route the proposal internally.

Kind regards,
Ragunauth Ramsaroop
Liaison Director, Social Responsibility
AGM Inc. | Zijin Mining Group
ragunauthramsaroop@icloud.com
ragunauthramsaroop.com

strategic_brief.title: Strategic Value Creation Proposal: Energy Strategy, Government Affairs and Emerging-Market Advisory
strategic_brief.executive_summary: Rystad Energy combines energy intelligence, market analysis and advisory work across a global client base. A further source of value lies in connecting analytical insight more directly to the institutional realities that shape project execution in emerging resource markets: government priorities, regulatory pathways, stakeholder expectations, local-content pressures, social-license issues and the practical delivery of energy-transition commitments. I bring director-level experience operating at this interface inside a multinational mining company in Guyana, one of the world's fastest-growing resource economies. My contribution would be to help convert policy, stakeholder and operating signals into sharper client advice, stronger country intelligence and practical strategic action.
strategic_brief.company_context: Rystad Energy is headquartered in Oslo and operates globally across energy research, data, analytics and advisory. Its leadership describes the business as an energy knowledge house serving energy companies, suppliers, financial institutions, governments and other stakeholders, with expertise spanning oil and gas, power, renewables, emissions, energy systems and strategy. The firm's careers platform also emphasizes experienced hires, multicultural teams and global leadership development across more than 20 countries. That model creates an opportunity to deepen the bridge between market intelligence and on-the-ground institutional execution, particularly in fast-changing resource economies where commercial outcomes depend on government relations, regulatory sequencing, stakeholder confidence, infrastructure constraints and credible sustainability governance as much as on market fundamentals.

opportunities.title: Emerging-market institutional intelligence
opportunities.rationale: Energy and resource projects in high-growth markets are shaped by ministries, regulators, state agencies, local-content expectations, investment frameworks and public legitimacy. Market analysis is stronger when those institutional variables are tracked as operating factors rather than treated only as external context.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would develop country-level institutional intelligence frameworks that connect policy developments, regulatory dependencies, stakeholder positions and execution constraints to commercial scenarios, client strategy and investment decision-making.

opportunities.title: Energy transition grounded in operating reality
opportunities.rationale: Clients increasingly need transition strategies that survive contact with infrastructure constraints, project economics, permitting, grid conditions, community expectations and operational evidence. This requires a practical bridge between high-level scenarios and implementation realities.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would bring operating-side experience from renewable-energy deployment, carbon-data governance and regulated industrial execution to strengthen advisory work on implementation risk, stakeholder alignment, evidence quality and transition sequencing.

opportunities.title: Government and stakeholder advisory
opportunities.rationale: Corporate clients often understand market direction but still struggle with how to engage governments, regulators and external stakeholders in a disciplined way. A structured stakeholder architecture can reduce surprises and improve the quality of strategic decisions.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would support advisory teams with stakeholder mapping, government-engagement strategy, commitment governance and issue escalation frameworks built from direct experience coordinating across ministries, regulators and operating functions.

opportunities.title: Client growth in resource economies
opportunities.rationale: Rystad Energy's global platform is well positioned to expand advisory relationships in mining-linked, oil-producing and energy-transition markets where clients need both macro intelligence and practical country-facing support. Guyana and similar markets offer a strong test case for this combined proposition.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would help identify senior client opportunities, frame country-specific value propositions and connect energy, mining, infrastructure and policy themes into executive-level advisory conversations with operators, investors and public institutions.

days_0_30: Map priority emerging-market clients and institutional issues where advisory value can be deepened.
Review current energy-transition and country-risk offerings for execution-level gaps.
days_31_60: Build a pilot institutional-intelligence framework linking policy, regulatory and stakeholder signals to client decisions.
Develop two or three market-specific executive propositions for priority resource economies.
days_61_90: Test the framework with selected advisory and commercial teams and convert live client issues into measurable outputs.
Establish an executive issue dashboard for high-value government, regulatory and stakeholder developments.
days_91_180: Scale the strongest methods across selected markets and client accounts.
Measure contribution through client engagement, advisory pipeline, repeat mandates and decision-useful country intelligence.

potential_impact: Stronger integration of institutional and stakeholder realities into energy-market advisory.
More practical transition advice for clients operating in regulated and infrastructure-constrained markets.
Higher-value executive engagement with governments, operators and investors in emerging resource economies.
Additional advisory and business-development pathways linking energy, mining, infrastructure and public policy.
background_relevance: Director-level responsibility spanning government relations, regulatory coordination, ESG, corporate affairs, social performance and executive advisory within a multinational mining operation.
Senior engagement across agencies responsible for mining, environment, energy, labour, aviation, standards, taxation, trade and investment, with cross-functional follow-through inside operations.
Experience supporting renewable-energy and carbon-data governance in a regulated industrial setting, including stakeholder coordination and evidence traceability.
Practical exposure to Guyana's rapid resource-sector growth and the institutional demands created by large-scale mining, energy, infrastructure and investment expansion.
